region.text: Ifriqiya and the central Maghreb round Ashir

ledger.note: 972: Buluggin ibn Ziri becomes viceroy of Ifriqiya for the Fatimids. 'After the Fatimids moved to Egypt in 972, he was appointed viceroy of Ifriqiya. On 2 October 972 at Sardaniya, his position was confirmed'; on 20 December he took up residence at Sabra al-Mansuriyya. Infobox 'Established: 972'. The state is nominally Fatimid until the 1040s.

region.text: Tripoli and its coast, the overlordship of Tripolitania

ledger.note: 978: the Fatimids grant Buluggin 'overlordship of Tripolitania'. The page names the region, not its rulers; the Tripoli district stands for it.

region.text: Fez, Sijilmasa and the western Maghreb

ledger.counterpart: western Maghreb rulers (not named on the page)
ledger.note: 980: Buluggin conquers Fez and the western Maghreb. 'By 980 he had conquered Fez and most of the western Maghreb'; he died at Sijilmasa in 984. The page does not name the rulers he displaced.

region.text: Fez, Sijilmasa and the western Maghreb

ledger.note: 985: Morocco abandoned. Buluggin 'died in Sijilmasa in 984, and his successor abandoned Morocco in 985'; no heir to the land is named.

region.text: the central Maghreb round Ashir, Zirid until Hammad's rebellion

ledger.note: 1015: Hammad rebels. 'Hammad rebelled in 1015 and declared independence' (the Hammadid page: independence 1014).

ledger.note: 1017: peace with Hammad. 'A 1017 peace agreement with al-Mu'izz ibn Badis let him keep effective independence.'

region.text: the central Maghreb round Ashir, Zirid until Hammad's rebellion

ledger.note: 1017: the central Maghreb round Ashir is lost to the Hammadids.

region.text: the interior of Ifriqiya between the coast and the Algerian border

ledger.note: 1052: the Zirids are routed by the Arab nomads. 'On 14 April 1052, the Battle of Haydaran was fought. The Zirids sent about 30,000 Sanhaja cavalry against roughly 3,000 Arab cavalry, and the Zirids were decisively defeated.' The interior is contested until Kairouan is given up in 1057.
1057: the interior is abandoned to the nomads (see the loss event); the contest ends because the Zirids no longer hold it.

1057: Kairouan abandoned. 'In 1057, al-Mu'izz ibn Badis abandoned Kairouan and moved the capital to Mahdia'; the Banu Hilal page: 'The Zirids abandoned Kairouan to take refuge on the coast where they survived for a century.' The lost interior is Cliopatria's 1056 shape minus its coastal 1066 shape.
1057: the capital moves from al-Mansuriyya to Mahdia.
1059: Tunis passes to the Banu Khurasan. 'Tunis was ruled by the Banu Khurasan dynasty, founded in 1059.'

1135: Jerba falls to the Normans. 'The island of Djerba was conquered by Roger II in 1135', Roger's 'first permanent conquest'; the Zirid page: 'Jerba fell in 1135'. That Jerba was Zirid is the Zirid page's context.

region.text: Tripoli and its coast, the overlordship of Tripolitania

ledger.note: 1146: the Norman capture of Tripoli ends whatever Zirid overlordship remained: 'In 1146 he successfully besieged it'. No page dates the end of the 978 grant, so the year is the researcher's bridge.
1148: Mahdia falls. 'When the Sicilians reached Mahdia on 22 June, the emir and his court fled the unprepared city' (George of Antioch's fleet). Mahdia had been 'a protectorate of Sicily by 1142'.
1148: Sousse surrenders on 1 July without a fight to the Norman fleet.

region.text: the coastal strip round Mahdia, Sousse, Sfax and Gabes

ledger.note: 1148: the Zirid dynasty ends with the fall of Sfax on 12 July. 'In 1148, the Normans captured Sfax, Gabes, and Mahdia'; 'On 12 July Sfax fell after short resistance'. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1148'. Gabes had asked Roger to make its ruler Yusuf a wali and was taken by the Almohads in 1159-60.

wars.name: Zirid-Hammadid War

zones.text: the central Maghreb round Ashir, Zirid until Hammad's rebellion

wars.outcome: Hammad's rebellion succeeds: a 1017 peace let him keep effective independence.

wars.name: Zirid intervention in Sicily
wars.outcome: 'In 1036, Sicilian Muslims asked al-Mu'izz for help against Kalbid emir al-Akhal. In 1038, al-Akhal was killed in Palermo, and the Zirid force withdrew that year.' A Zirid fleet of 400 ships was lost off Pantelleria in 1025 (or 1021). No land changed hands.

wars.name: Battle of Haydaran and the Hilalian invasion
wars.outcome: Zirid defeat at Haydaran on 14 April 1052; Kairouan abandoned in 1057; the dynasty survives on the coast at Mahdia.

wars.name: Norman conquest of the Zirid coast
wars.outcome: Djerba 1135, Mahdia a protectorate of Sicily by 1142, Tripoli 1146, Mahdia 22 June 1148, Sousse 1 July, Sfax 12 July; the Zirid dynasty ends in 1148.

wars.name: Zirid conquest of the western Maghreb
belligerents: western Maghreb rulers (not named on the page)
wars.outcome: 'By 980 he had conquered Fez and most of the western Maghreb'; Buluggin died at Sijilmasa in 984 and 'his successor abandoned Morocco in 985'.
wars.note: The page names no opponent; the second belligerent is a placeholder.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines on the pages opened: the interior of Ifriqiya was nomad and Hilalian country after 1052, the Ashir frontier was a governorate boundary until 1015, and the coast is the only fixed edge.

notes: Start 972, not Cliopatria's 1056: the Zirid page puts the dynasty's establishment in 972 (viceroy of Ifriqiya for the Fatimids). Cliopatria's Fatimid Caliphate shapes 970-1055 contain Ifriqiya (and in 1015-1017 reach 0.47W, in 980-1014 0.39W), so this dossier's new 972-1055 keyframes overlap the Fatimid row; the Fatimid dossier should draw Zirid Ifriqiya as a viceroyalty or client 972-c.1048 or the two will claim the same cells. The Zirid dynasty also ruled the Ashir country before 1015 (infobox: Ashir 936-1014), which is taken here as part of the 972-1014 shape. Ashir as a place is not in the gazetteer; the Hammadid 1018 outline stands for it. The 1040s break with the Fatimids is dated 'between 1041 and 1051', '1048-49' and 'the 1040s' on the page; no ledger type fits it, so it is recorded only in keyframe 1015 and here. Cliopatria's 1066-1146 shape includes Tunis, which the page gives to the Banu Khurasan from 1059 and the Hammadid page to Hammadid governors 1128-1148; Tunis is cut out of the corrections. The Zirid page does not say who held Tunis in 1148. Page conflicts: Hammad's rebellion 1014 (Hammadid page) vs 1015 (Zirid page); Buluggin's reign 973-984 (infobox) vs 971-984 (text); Mahdia fell in 1148, not 1152 or 1151 as Cliopatria's row end implies; the Almohad conquest of Mahdia is 1160 (Zirid page) or January 1160 (Kingdom of Africa page) and belongs to the Normans, not the Zirids. Not drawn: Jerba before 1135 as a distinct unit; Gabes (its ruler was a Norman client in 1148); Sardinia/Sicily links (a Zirid fleet was lost off Pantelleria in 1025 or 1021; the Zirid force left Sicily in 1038). The Zirid page has a 1074 raid on Calabria and the 1075 capture of Mazara (undated owner) which are not entered. Counterparts without a dossier: Banu Khurasan of Tunis (1059-1128); Banu Hilal and Banu Sulaym (a migration, not a state). Rulers not entered: the page names Buluggin (infobox 973-984), Badis, Hammad, al-Mu'izz ibn Badis and al-Hasan but the part read gives no complete list with reign years. Method note: every page was read through WebFetch, which returns a model-made extraction; phrases in quotation marks are the extraction's wording of the page and may differ in small ways from the live text, while the years and months are the ones it reported.
